recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. Related subjectType and section/item-subject issues should be audited separately if needed; they do not require changing the base QuestionnaireResponse.subject scope for FHIR-3015.
issue_request: FHIR-3015 was a Published FHIR-core Patient Care change request with a Persuasive with Modification resolution. It questioned limiting Questionnaire/QuestionnaireAnswers subject to Patient|RelatedPerson when questionnaires may concern devices, medications, organizations, practitioners, and other resources, and the recorded resolution was to change subject from Patient|RelatedPerson to Any.
initial_application: No explicit FHIR-3015-tagged commit was found. The likely application is the early Questionnaire split in commit 54ddc30bbb, which removed the old Questionnaire.subject Reference(Patient|RelatedPerson) row and introduced QuestionnaireAnswers.subject as Resource(Any) with broad subject text. Later FHIR-6044 added Questionnaire.subjectType because QuestionnaireAnswers.subject was Reference(Any), and the QuestionnaireAnswers to QuestionnaireResponse rename preserved that model.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini actively includes Questionnaire and QuestionnaireResponse. Current Questionnaire.subjectType is optional and says that if none are specified the subject is unlimited. Current QuestionnaireResponse.subject targets Resource and says the subject could be a patient, organization, practitioner, device, etc.; FHIR-11004 later clarified that a declared Questionnaire.subjectType constrains QuestionnaireResponse.subject. Searches found no current Questionnaire.subject or Patient|RelatedPerson subject restriction in the build-scope Questionnaire/QuestionnaireResponse source, and no relevant Zulip or Confluence conflict.
reconciliation: No source change was made because the current source already represents the unrestricted base subject model requested by FHIR-3015 while retaining optional Questionnaire.subjectType narrowing for specific questionnaires.

related_jiras.note: Added Questionnaire.subjectType after noting QuestionnaireAnswers.subject was Reference(Any), providing the optional type constraint used today.
Clarified that Questionnaire.subjectType limits QuestionnaireResponse.subject when declared, supporting current source wording.
Answered that Questionnaire is not linked to patient/related person and QuestionnaireAnswers can link to Patient, RelatedPerson, or anything else.
Discusses group/section subject handling rather than the base QuestionnaireResponse.subject scope, so it was not decided here.

evidence_items.summary: Published/Persuasive with Modification FHIR-core issue asking why Questionnaire/QuestionnaireAnswers subject was limited to Patient|RelatedPerson and recording a resolution to change it to Any.
evidence_items.learned: This establishes the seed decision: the base questionnaire answer/response subject should not be limited to Patient and RelatedPerson.

evidence_items.summary: Questionnaire and QuestionnaireResponse are active resources; Questionnaire.subjectType is optional and unlimited when absent; QuestionnaireResponse.subject is Reference(Resource).
evidence_items.learned: The current build-scope source already permits any QuestionnaireResponse subject unless a particular Questionnaire declares subjectType.

evidence_items.summary: Early Questionnaire split commit removed the old Questionnaire.subject Reference(Patient|RelatedPerson) model and introduced QuestionnaireAnswers.subject as Resource(Any) with broad subject definition text.
evidence_items.learned: This is the likely historical application of FHIR-3015 despite the absence of an explicit issue key in the commit message.

evidence_items.summary: FHIR-6044 added Questionnaire.subjectType because QuestionnaireAnswers.subject was Reference(Any), and FHIR-11004 clarified that subjectType constrains QuestionnaireResponse.subject when declared.
evidence_items.learned: Later related decisions preserve the unrestricted base subject while allowing Questionnaire authors to declare narrower subject types.
